Create dimensioned printable hardware with fit checks and a simple size selector.
Dimensions in mm. The bolt has an external helical thread approximated for FDM printing.
The nut includes a matching helical internal thread. Radial clearance compensates for printer tolerances.
Flat washer. The selected metric size controls the starting hole diameter.
Creates one screw and three comparison nuts: tight bottom right, balanced top left, loose top right. The screw is bottom left.
Fit depends on printer calibration and material. Print a small fit sample first; use about 0.3–0.5 mm extra for clearance bores.
Simplified metric coarse threads for FDM. Set the screw and nut to the same size and pitch. Print a fit sample before making load-bearing parts.

Make a backlit photo panel or a printable open-top cube kit. For a cube, select exactly four photos. The STL contains four image panels and a square base, arranged flat for printing and glue assembly.
Select exactly four photos to build the lithophane cube.
Image %1$d of %2$d: Choose the next photo.
Maximum wall thickness must be greater than the minimum.
The framed lithophane is a 3D model. Select STL as the output format.
Check the frame thickness, stand depth and cable opening dimensions.
Relief preview · bright areas print thinner; dark areas print thicker
Create a printable plate with raised text. Choose dimensions, lettering height and an optional keyring hole. The text is converted locally into real 3D geometry.
Enter some text for the nameplate.
Create a hollow storage box and a matching slip-over lid. The lid is laid beside the box for printing. An optional round cable opening passes through the box floor.
Make a C-shaped clip with an open mouth so the cable snaps in from the side. The optional mounting tab with screw hole is printed as one piece. Measure the cable and leave a little clearance.
Clip wall thickness must be 1.2–6 mm.
The clip opening must be at least 40% of the cable diameter and smaller than the cable.
Mounting tab length must be 8–40 mm.
The screw hole must be 0–9.9 mm and fit inside the mounting tab.

Create a hollow cable sleeve with a square flange and two screw ears for mounting to a desk or enclosure. The center and both screw holes remain open through the part. Measure the cable and desk thickness before printing.
Tube wall thickness must be 1.2–6 mm.
The flange must be 30–100 mm wide and clear the tube wall by at least 5 mm.
Tube length below the desk must be 8–60 mm.
Screw hole diameter must be 2.5–8 mm.

Create a screw-mounted tool rail with tall guide sleeves. The sleeves guide screwdrivers or drill bits so they do not slide out of a thin plate. Print the rail flat, then mount it to the wall at two points.
Mounting plate thickness must be 2–6 mm.
Mounting screw holes must be 3–8 mm.
Tool guide sleeves must be 6–35 mm high.
Create a tapered planter and saucer
Make a hollow tapered pot with a drain opening and an optional matching drip saucer. Pot and saucer are arranged separately on the plate in one STL.
The pot bottom diameter must be 30–180 mm.
The pot opening diameter must be 30–200 mm.
The pot height must be 20–220 mm.
The pot wall must be 1.2–5 mm.
The pot floor must be 1.5–8 mm.
The drain must be 2–20 mm and smaller than the free pot floor.
Saucer wall thickness must be 1.2–6 mm.
Saucer wall height must be 4–25 mm.
Saucer floor thickness must be 1.2–5 mm.
Create a set of plant markers
Enter one plant name per line. Up to eight raised-text markers are arranged in two columns as separate printable pieces in one STL.
Plant names · one per line, up to 8
Check the marker names and dimensions
Enter 1–8 plant names, one per line.
Each plant name can contain up to 24 characters.
Raised text height must be 0.4–4 mm.
Stake hole must be zero or no wider than half of the shorter side of the marker.
The marker set would exceed 200 mm. Reduce marker size or use fewer names.
Create a one-piece stand with a leaned back support, front retaining lip and an open cable route. Adjust it to your device. Prints flat on the base; the support rib is part of the same model.
Back support height must be 50–140 mm.
Front lip height must be 8–28 mm.
Cable opening must be 8–30 mm and leave at least 20 mm on each side.
Cable channel must be 12–40 mm and leave at least 18 mm of base.
These angle and depth values leave too little room for the front device support.
Create an under-desk power strip holder

Create a flat-printable tray to screw under a desk or shelf. Low side rails and end stops hold the power strip; four mounting holes secure the tray. A centered rear notch leaves room for the power cable.
Check the power strip holder dimensions
Power strip body length must be 80–300 mm.
Power strip body width must be 30–100 mm.
Power strip body height must be 10–60 mm.
Tray floor thickness must be 2–6 mm.
End stops must be 8–25 mm high.
Cable notch must be 8–30 mm and at least 10 mm narrower than the inside width.
Mounting screw holes must be 3–8 mm.
